text:
B: Hello. Can you hear me all right?
A: Yeah. Tracey.
B: Carys. Nice to meet you.
A: And you. Your kitchen's very tidy, I noticed that on the photo.
B: Oh. Thank you. It's not usually, I tidied the bit the camera can see.
A: That's what I did and all. The post's still there though.
B: I saw the takeaway calendar. That's a proper kitchen, that.
A: Friday nights. So what do you do?
B: Civil engineer. Flood risk, drainage, that sort of thing. For councils, mostly. And you?
A: Kitchen assistant in a primary school canteen. Veg prep, the hatch, washing up. Is that what you wanted?
B: Yes, that's fine. Do you like it?
A: It's alright. Term-time suits me. I'll stay there till I can afford to stop, if my knees hold out.
B: That's a plan, to be fair.
A: My dad worked at Ford in Dagenham, and when it wound down he never really got over it. So I like knowing where I am.
B: My dad was at Shotton. The steelworks. Same thing, really. He was never quite the same after.
A: No. They weren't, were they. That generation.
B: No.
A: Is he still about, your dad?
B: He is, yes. Mum and dad are both near me. Mum helps with Rhys, my son, more than I'd like her to have to.
A: My mum's seventy-eight. She's getting forgetful. Left the gas on last month. I go round Sundays with my sister but it's the other six days I lie awake about.
B: That must be hard.
A: It is. Sorry, I don't normally say all that to people.
B: No, it's fine. I'd rather that than talking about the weather.
A: You'd be good at the weather though, with floods.
B: I'm awful about the weather. I check river levels before bed.
A: Do you? That's mad. I check Facebook for old photos of Dagenham.
B: Each to their own. What do you do when you're not working?
A: Walk round Parsloes Park. Puzzle pages, word searches. And true crime, which I shouldn't, cos it gives me the creeps and then I can't sleep.
B: I read crime novels. Same problem, really, I'll be up till one finishing one.
A: Steve says turn it off and I say no, I need to know who done it.
B: Yeah, no, you can't stop halfway. That's the whole point of it.
A: Did you like the puzzle at the start?
B: I did, actually. I do the Saturday cryptic, so I'm used to it.
A: I can't do them cryptic ones. I don't see how anyone gets them.
B: Honestly, it took me years. I still get stuck on one clue all week sometimes. I've just finished one that drove me mad.
A: Well, you sound sensible. You seem it and all.
B: Thank you. So do you, if that's any help.
A: It is a bit.
